notes.summary: This topic covers the basic parts of a computer (input, CPU, memory, output), the types of memory and their units, and number systems. Tier 2 asks 4–6 direct, one-line questions here, so learn the facts and the conversions.

concepts.title: Parts of a computer
concepts.body:
Every computer follows the Input → Process → Output cycle.
  • CPU (the "brain") has the Control Unit (directs all operations) and the ALU (does arithmetic and logic). Registers are tiny, very fast storage inside the CPU.
  • Input devices: keyboard, mouse, scanner, light pen, joystick, microphone, OMR, MICR, barcode reader.
  • Output devices: monitor, printer, plotter, speaker, projector.

concepts.title: Types of memory
concepts.body:
• Primary memory: RAM (volatile, read-write, loses data when power goes) and ROM (non-volatile, holds the BIOS/firmware). Types of ROM: PROM, EPROM (erased by UV light), EEPROM (erased electrically).
  • Cache: very fast memory between CPU and RAM.
  • Secondary memory: HDD, SSD, pen drive, CD/DVD; non-volatile and large.
Speed order (fastest first): Register > Cache > RAM > SSD > HDD. Cost per byte follows the same order.

concepts.title: Memory units
concepts.body:
1 nibble = 4 bits; 1 byte = 8 bits.
1 KB = 1024 bytes; 1 MB = 1024 KB; 1 GB = 1024 MB; 1 TB = 1024 GB; 1 PB = 1024 TB.
So 1 KB = 210 bytes, 1 MB = 220, 1 GB = 230, 1 TB = 240 bytes.

concepts.title: Number systems
concepts.body:
SystemBaseDigits
Binary20, 1
Octal80–7
Decimal100–9
Hexadecimal160–9, A–F (A = 10 … F = 15)
To convert to decimal, multiply each digit by the place value (power of the base) and add.

varieties.name: Hardware and devices
varieties.how: Know the CPU parts and classify each device as input, output or storage.

example.q: Which unit of the CPU performs addition and comparison?
steps: Arithmetic (addition) and logic (comparison) are done by the Arithmetic Logic Unit.
The Control Unit only directs; it does not calculate.

varieties.name: Memory types and units
varieties.how: Remember volatile vs non-volatile, the speed order, and that each unit is 1024 times the previous one.

example.q: How many KB are there in 2 MB?

varieties.name: Number system conversion
varieties.how: Write place values (powers of the base) from the right, multiply by each digit and add.

tips: For hex, remember A = 10, B = 11, C = 12, D = 13, E = 14, F = 15.
Group binary digits in 3s for octal and in 4s for hexadecimal conversion.
BIOS is stored in ROM; the operating system is loaded into RAM during booting.
traps: 1 KB is 1024 bytes in computer memory questions, not 1000.
Plotter and speaker are output devices; light pen and joystick are input devices.
Cache is faster than RAM but registers are faster than cache.

questions.q: Which part of a computer is called its "brain"?
questions.solution: The Central Processing Unit (CPU) controls and processes all instructions, so it is called the brain of the computer.

questions.q: Which memory loses its contents when the power is switched off?
questions.solution: RAM is volatile memory. ROM, EPROM and hard disk are non-volatile and keep data without power.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an input device?
questions.solution: A plotter draws large graphics on paper, so it is an output device. Scanner, light pen and joystick send data into the computer.

questions.q: Which of these is the fastest memory?
questions.solution: Speed order: Registers > Cache > RAM > SSD. Registers are inside the CPU itself, so they are the fastest.

questions.q: The binary number (1011)<sub>2</sub> is equal to which decimal number?
The hexadecimal number (2F)<sub>16</sub> is equal to which decimal number?
A memory of 4 GB is equal to how many MB?

flashcards.back: Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), plus registers
Ultraviolet (UV) light. EEPROM is erased electrically.
